ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
At each of the sixteen circles in the network below stands a student. A total of 3360 coins are distributed among the sixteen students. All at once, all students give away all their coins by passing an equal number of coins to each of their neighbors in the network. After the trade, all students have the same number of coins as they started with. Find the number of coins the student standing at the center circle had originally.

Reasoning: Let the original number of coins at a certain vertex be x_v, and its degree be d_v. Each student gives all coins equally to adjacent students, which is equivalent to the coins making one step of a simple random walk on the undirected graph. The distribution after the transaction is unchanged, so the original distribution is the stationary distribution of this random walk. The stationary distribution of a connected undirected graph is proportional to the vertex degrees, so the number of coins at each vertex should be the same constant multiplied by that vertex's degree. The total number of coins 3360 corresponds to the total degree 60, so each degree corresponds to 3360/60=56 coins. The center dot has degree 5, so the original number of coins of the center student is 5×56=280.

method.method_draft: Read the graph from the image: it has 16 circles, the central circle is joined to 5 neighboring circles, and the whole network has 30 edges total, so the sum of all vertex degrees is 60. From the text, each student gives all coins equally among adjacent students and the distribution is unchanged after the simultaneous trade. Model one coin as making one step of a random walk on this undirected graph. An unchanged distribution is a stationary distribution for the simple random walk. For a connected undirected graph, the stationary amount at a vertex is proportional to its degree. Therefore the center originally had 5/60 of the total 3360 coins, giving 3360 * 5 / 60 = 280.

method.method_draft: First read the network in the image: it is connected, the central circle has 5 incident edges, and there are 30 edges in all. Let p_v be the number of coins student v gives to each neighbor; then the original coins at v are d_v p_v, where d_v is the degree of v. From the text's unchanged-after-trade condition, d_v p_v equals the sum of p_u over all neighbors u of v, so p_v is the average of the neighboring p-values. Since the graph is connected, a finite harmonic function with each value equal to the average of its neighbors must be constant, so every p_v is the same value c. Thus the original number of coins at each vertex equals c times its degree. The total is c times the total degree 60, so c = 3360/60 = 56. The center has degree 5, so it had 5c = 280 coins.
